content: The medication combination of aluminum hydroxide, magnesium hydroxide, and simethicone can be administered as follows: take 10-20 mL orally every 4-6 hours, either 1 hour before or 3 hours after meals. Alternatively, chew 2-4 tablets every 4-6 hours, but do not exceed 12 tablets in a 24-hour period. The safety and efficacy of this regimen have not been fully established. Drug Interactions: 1. Pazopanib: Aluminum hydroxide increases gastric pH, reducing pazopanib's absorption and effectiveness. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both drugs. Co-administration is contraindicated. Short-acting antacids may be used instead of proton pump inhibitors (PPIs) or H2 antagonists, but pazopanib and antacid doses should be separated by several hours. 2. Raltegravir: Aluminum hydroxide binds to raltegravir in the gastrointestinal (GI) tract, reducing its levels. Co-administration is contraindicated, even with dose separation. 3. Atazanavir: Aluminum hydroxide increases gastric pH, reducing atazanavir's solubility and plasma concentrations. Administer atazanavir 2 hours before or 1 hour after aluminum hydroxide. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 4. Baloxavir Marboxil: Aluminum and magnesium hydroxide bind to baloxavir in the GI tract, reducing its absorption. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. Studies in monkeys have shown significant reductions in plasma levels when co-administered with calcium, aluminum, or iron. 5. Ciprofloxacin: Aluminum and magnesium hydroxide inhibit ciprofloxacin absorption in the GI tract, reducing its bioavailability by up to 90%. Administer ciprofloxacin at least 2 hours before or 6 hours after antacids. Use alternatives if available. 6. Demeclocycline: Magnesium hydroxide inhibits demeclocycline absorption in the GI tract. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. Separate doses by 2 hours. 7. Dapsone: Aluminum hydroxide increases gastric pH, reducing dapsone's absorption. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 8. Dasatinib: Aluminum hydroxide increases gastric pH, reducing dasatinib's absorption. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 9. Digoxin: Aluminum hydroxide increases digoxin levels by altering gastric pH. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 10. Doxycycline: Aluminum and magnesium hydroxide inhibit doxycycline absorption in the GI tract. Separate doses by 2 hours. 11. Eltrombopag: Aluminum and magnesium hydroxide inhibit eltrombopag absorption in the GI tract. Co-administration is contraindicated. Separate doses by at least 4 hours. 12. Fleroxacin: Aluminum and magnesium hydroxide inhibit fleroxacin absorption in the GI tract. Separate doses by 2 hours. 13. Infigratinib: Aluminum and magnesium hydroxide inhibit infigratinib absorption in the GI tract. Avoid or use an alternative drug. If unavoidable, administer infigratinib 2 hours before and after antacids. 14. Gemifloxacin: Aluminum and magnesium hydroxide inhibit gemifloxacin absorption in the GI tract. Separate doses by 2 hours. 15. Sotorasib: Simethicone inhibits sotorasib absorption in the GI tract. Avoid or use an alternative drug. If unavoidable, administer sotorasib 4 hours before or 10 hours after antacids. 16. Acalabrutinib: Aluminum hydroxide increases gastric pH, reducing acalabrutinib's solubility. Separate doses by at least 2 hours. 17. Acebutolol: Aluminum hydroxide inhibits acebutolol absorption in the GI tract. Separate doses by 2 hours. 18. Alendronate: Aluminum hydroxide inhibits alendronate absorption in the GI tract. Separate doses by 2 hours. 19. Allopurinol: Aluminum hydroxide inhibits allopurinol absorption in the GI tract. Separate doses by 2 hours. 20. Amphetamine: Aluminum hydroxide increases amphetamine levels by altering renal tubular reabsorption. Use caution and monitor closely. 21. Atenolol: Aluminum hydroxide inhibits atenolol absorption in the GI tract. Separate doses by 2 hours. 22. Azithromycin: Aluminum hydroxide inhibits azithromycin absorption in the GI tract. Separate doses by 2 hours. 23. Bearberry: Aluminum hydroxide increases bearberry levels by altering renal tubular reabsorption. Use caution and monitor closely. 24. Benazepril: Aluminum hydroxide may reduce benazepril absorption. Use caution and monitor closely. 25. Betaxolol: Aluminum hydroxide inhibits betaxolol absorption in the GI tract. Separate doses by 2 hours. 26. Bictegravir: Aluminum and magnesium hydroxide bind to bictegravir in the GI tract, reducing its levels. Administer bictegravir 2 hours before or 6 hours after antacids. Routine simultaneous administration is not recommended. 27. Bisoprolol: Aluminum hydroxide inhibits bisoprolol absorption in the GI tract. Separate doses by 2 hours. 28. Cabotegravir: Aluminum and magnesium hydroxide bind to cabotegravir in the GI tract, reducing its levels. Administer antacids at least 2 hours before or 4 hours after cabotegravir. 29. Bosutinib: Aluminum hydroxide increases gastric pH, reducing bosutinib's solubility. Use short-acting antacids with a 2-hour separation. 30. Budesonide: Aluminum hydroxide increases gastric pH, potentially causing premature dissolution of extended-release budesonide tablets. Monitor closely. 31. Capecitabine: Aluminum hydroxide enhances capecitabine absorption. Use caution and monitor closely. 32. Captopril: Aluminum hydroxide may reduce captopril absorption. Use caution and monitor closely. 33. Carbonyl Iron: Aluminum hydroxide increases gastric pH, reducing carbonyl iron absorption. Use caution and monitor closely. 34. Carvedilol: Aluminum hydroxide inhibits carvedilol absorption in the GI tract. Separate doses by 2 hours. 35. Cefdinir: Aluminum hydroxide increases gastric pH, reducing cefdinir absorption. Use caution and monitor closely. 36. Cefditoren: Aluminum hydroxide increases gastric pH, reducing cefditoren absorption. Use caution and monitor closely. 37. Cefpodoxime: Aluminum hydroxide increases gastric pH, reducing cefpodoxime absorption. Use caution and monitor closely. 38. Cefuroxime: Aluminum hydroxide increases gastric pH, reducing cefuroxime absorption. Use caution and monitor closely. 39. Celecoxib: Aluminum hydroxide inhibits celecoxib absorption in the GI tract. Separate doses by 2 hours. 40. Celiprolol: Aluminum hydroxide inhibits celiprolol absorption in the GI tract. Separate doses by 2 hours. 41. Chenodiol: Aluminum hydroxide inhibits chenodiol absorption in the GI tract. Separate doses by 2 hours. 42. Chloroquine: Aluminum and magnesium hydroxide inhibit chloroquine absorption in the GI tract. Separate doses by at least 4 hours. 43. Cholic Acid: Aluminum hydroxide binds to cholic acid in the GI tract. Take cholic acid at least 1 hour before or 4-6 hours after aluminum-based antacids. 44. Crizotinib: Aluminum and magnesium hydroxide increase gastric pH, reducing crizotinib's solubility. Use caution and monitor closely. 45. Cyclosporine: Aluminum hydroxide inhibits cyclosporine absorption in the GI tract. Separate doses by 2 hours. 46. Deferiprone: Aluminum hydroxide binds to deferiprone in the GI tract. Separate doses by at least 4 hours. 47. Deferasirox: Avoid co-administration of deferasirox with aluminum-containing antacids. 48. Delafloxacin: Aluminum hydroxide binds to delafloxacin in the GI tract. Administer delafloxacin at least 2 hours before or 6 hours after antacids. 49. Dextroamphetamine: Aluminum hydroxide increases dextroamphetamine levels by altering renal tubular reabsorption. Use caution and monitor closely. 50. Dolutegravir: Aluminum and magnesium hydroxide bind to dolutegravir in the GI tract. Administer dolutegravir 2 hours before or 6 hours after antacids. 51. Elvitegravir: Aluminum hydroxide reduces elvitegravir levels by forming ionic complexes in the GI tract. Separate doses by at least 2 hours. 52. Erythromycin: Aluminum hydroxide increases erythromycin levels by an unknown mechanism. Use caution and monitor closely. 53. Esomeprazole: Aluminum hydroxide inhibits esomeprazole absorption in the GI tract. Separate doses by 2 hours. 54. Ethambutol: Avoid administering aluminum hydroxide-containing antacids for at least 4 hours following ethambutol. 55. Etidronate: Aluminum hydroxide inhibits etidronate absorption in the GI tract.
